subject: Business
title: Porter's Five Forces
description: A fast breakdown of Porter's Five Forces for builders.

hook.text: Why are airlines barely profitable while software companies mint money? Michael Porter has the answer.

buildup.text: Five forces shape every industry's profitability: rivalry, new entrants, substitutes, buyers, and suppliers.

discovery.text: Airlines face brutal rivalry, low switching costs, and powerful suppliers (Boeing, fuel). Profits evaporate.

twist.text: Software has high switching costs, few substitutes, and weak buyer power. The forces protect profits.

climax.text: Strategy isn't just about beating competitors. It's about choosing an industry where the forces favor you.

punchline.text: Don't just win the game. Pick a game you can win.

quiz.question: What are Porter's Five Forces designed to assess?
options: The competitive forces shaping an industry's profitability
A company's internal strengths and weaknesses
The best marketing channels for a product

details.summary: Porter's Five Forces analyzes industry profitability by examining five competitive dynamics: threat of new entrants, bargaining power of suppliers, bargaining power of buyers, threat of substitutes, and rivalry among existing competitors. Strong forces reduce industry profitability.
details.whyItMatters: The Five Forces framework explains why some industries are consistently profitable while others are not. It helps businesses assess industry attractiveness before entering and identify which forces to address strategically to improve their position.
takeaways: Five competitive forces determine industry profitability potential
Strong forces squeeze margins while weak forces allow higher profits
Strategy should reduce the most threatening forces or exploit favorable ones

faq.question: How do the five forces differ from SWOT analysis?
faq.answer: Five Forces analyzes the industry structure to determine profit potential for any player. SWOT analyzes a specific company's position within that industry. Five Forces is external industry-level analysis. SWOT combines external conditions with internal company capabilities.

faq.question: Which of the five forces is typically most important?
faq.answer: It varies by industry. In commodities, buyer power dominates. In technology, threat of substitutes and new entrants matter most. In pharmaceuticals, supplier power from patent holders is critical. The framework helps identify which force most impacts your specific industry's profitability.
